notes:

H. Kovacs presented the report and responded to questions from the Committee. J. Silcox Childs and J. Shea, were also in attendance to respond to questions from the Committee.

motions.item_title: Administrative Monetary Penalty System - Increased Penalty fines for Parking Violations, CSD-2024-431
motions.text: it was resolved: "That Council approve Schedule "A" under the Administrative Monetary Penalty System (AMPS) to increase penalty fines for parking violations as outlined in Community Services Department report CSD-2024-431."
motions.text_html:
it was resolved:

"That Council approve Schedule "A" under the Administrative Monetary Penalty System (AMPS) to increase penalty fines for parking violations as outlined in Community Services Department report CSD-2024-431."

motions.item_title: Updates to the Public Tree By-law, INS-2025-190
motions.text: it was resolved: "That Chapter 690 (Public Tree Bylaw) (By-law 87-293) of the City of Kitchener Municipal Code be repealed and replaced with the proposed Public Tree Bylaw, as outlined in Infrastructure Services Staff report INS-2025-190 Attachment "A"; and, That the Clerk be authorized to update Chapter 690 (Public Tree By-law) of the City of Kitchener Municipal Code to reflect the proposed changes; and, That the Administrative Penalty By-law Fines for Public Tree Bylaw, as noted in Attachment "B" of staff report INS-2025-190, be approved; and further, That staff be directed to implement the new bylaw, including necessary education, enforcement, and monitoring measures, to ensure compliance and the long-term health of the City’s urban forest."
motions.text_html:
it was resolved:

"That Chapter 690 (Public Tree Bylaw) (By-law 87-293) of the City of Kitchener Municipal Code be repealed and replaced with the proposed Public Tree Bylaw, as outlined in Infrastructure Services Staff report INS-2025-190 Attachment "A"; and,

That the Clerk be authorized to update Chapter 690 (Public Tree By-law) of the City of Kitchener Municipal Code to reflect the proposed changes; and,

That the Administrative Penalty By-law Fines for Public Tree Bylaw, as noted in Attachment "B" of staff report INS-2025-190, be approved; and further,

That staff be directed to implement the new bylaw, including necessary education, enforcement, and monitoring measures, to ensure compliance and the long-term health of the City’s urban forest."
